text:
Nvidia’s market value crossed $4 trillion on July 9, 2025, driven primarily by strong demand for its Blackwell accelerator rack systems (specifically GB200 and GB300) [Source: ev-1]. This surge was further fueled by the Stargate project’s approximately $500 billion AI-infrastructure plan and repeatedly raised capital expenditure guidance from major hyperscalers including Microsoft, Meta, Google, and Amazon throughout 2025 [Source: ev-1]. At this milestone, Nvidia held a dominant share of the AI-accelerator market, with its stock price crossing roughly $160 per share as CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the industry's transition from training to inference demand, describing "AI factories" selling compute as a commodity [Source: ev-1].

This milestone indicates that the market is pricing AI infrastructure as the largest new capital cycle since the internet era, effectively treating Nvidia as the primary "toll-booth" for this spending supercycle [Source: ev-1]. The rapid valuation trajectory—from $1 trillion in mid-2023 to $4 trillion by July 2025—underscores the scale of current investment, though it also highlights risks related to concentration, evidenced by Nvidia’s record weight in the S&P 500 and its rotation within the "$4T club" alongside Apple (which touched $4 trillion intraday on July 8, 2025) and Microsoft during 2025 [Source: ev-1].
